title: Erdos10.erdos_10
statement: True ↔ ∃ k, Erdos10.sumPrimeAndTwoPows k = Set.univ \ {0, 1}
summary:
Is there some $k$ such that every integer is the sum of a prime and at most $k$
powers of $2$?

title: Erdos100.erdos_100
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ C > 0,
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))), A.card = n → Erdos100.DistancesSeparated A → Metric.diam ↑A > C * ↑n
summary: Is the diameter of $A$ at least $Cn$ for some constant $C > 0$?

title: Erdos1003.erdos_1003
statement: True ↔ {n | n.totient = (n + 1).totient}.Infinite
summary:
Are there infinitely many solutions to $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$, where $\phi$ is the Euler totient
function?

title: Erdos1004.erdos_1004
statement: True ↔ ∀ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ n ≤ x, Erdos1004.IsDistinctTotientRun n ⌊Real.log ↑x ^ c⌋₊
summary:
For any fixed c > 0, if x is sufficiently large then there exists n ≤ x such that
the values of φ(n+k) are all distinct for 1 ≤ k ≤ (log x)^c.
This is an open problem.

title: Erdos1049.erdos_1049
statement: True ↔ ∀ t > 1, Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ+), 1 / (↑t ^ ↑n - 1))
summary:
Let $t>1$ be a rational number. Is
$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{1}{t^n-1}=\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\tau(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where
$\tau(n)$ counts the divisors of $n$?

A conjecture of Chowla.

title: Erdos1056.erdos_1056
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 2,
    ∃ p, ∃ (_ : Nat.Prime p), ∃ boundaries, ∃ (_ : StrictMono boundaries), Erdos1056.AllModProdEqualsOne p boundaries
summary:
Let $k ≥ 2$. Does there exist a prime $p$ and consecutive intervals $I_0,\dots,I_k$
such that $\prod\limits_{n{\in}I_i}n \equiv 1 \mod n$ for all $1 \le i \le k$?

title: Erdos1057.erdos_1057
statement: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto (fun x => Real.log (Erdos1057.carmichaelCounting x) / Real.log x) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)
summary:
Is it true that $C(x)=x^{1-o(1)}$?

This is discussed in problem A13 of Guy's collection [Gu04].

title: Erdos1060.erdos_1060.parts.ii
statement:
∃ C,
  (fun n => ↑{k ∈ Finset.Iic n | k * (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) k = n}.card) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => Real.log ↑n ^ C
summary: Part (ii) of Erdős Problem 1060: bound on the number of $k \le n$ with $k \sigma_1(k) = n$.

title: Erdos1062.erdos_1062.parts.ii
statement: (∃ l, Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos1062.f n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop (nhds l) ∧ Irrational l) ↔ True
summary:
Erdős asked whether the limiting density `f n / n` exists and, if so, whether it is
irrational.

title: Erdos1068.erdos_1068
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
    G.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1 → ∃ s, s.Countable ∧ (SimpleGraph.induce s G).InfinitelyConnected
summary:
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain a countable subgraph which is
infinitely connected?

title: Erdos1072.erdos_1072.parts.i
statement: True ↔ {p | Nat.Prime p ∧ Erdos1072.f p = p - 1}.Infinite
summary: Is it true that there are infinitely many $p$ for which $f(p) = p − 1$?

title: Erdos1072.erdos_1072.parts.ii
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ P ⊆ {p | Nat.Prime p},
    P.HasDensity 1 {p | Nat.Prime p} ∧
      Filter.Tendsto (fun p => ↑(Erdos1072.f p) / ↑p) (Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal P) (nhds 0)
summary: Is it true that $f(p)/p \to 0$ for $p \to \infty$ in a density 1 subset of the primes?

title: Erdos1073.erdos_1073
statement: True ↔ ∃ o, o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ (x : ℕ), Erdos1073.A x ≤ ↑x ^ o x
summary: Is it true that $A(x) \le x^{o(1)}$?

display_title: Erdős problem 1074 - EHS Numbers one half
title: Erdos1074.erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_one_half
statement: Erdos1074.EHSNumbers.HasDensity (1 / 2)
summary:
Regarding the first question, Hardy and Subbarao computed all EHS numbers up to $2^{10}$, and
write "...if this trend conditions we expect [the limit] to be around 0.5, if it exists."

title: Erdos108.erdos_108
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ r ≥ 4,
    ∀ k ≥ 2,
      ∃ f,
        ∀ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V),
          Nonempty V → ↑f ≤ G.chromaticNumber → ∃ H, H.coe.girth ≥ r ∧ H.coe.chromaticNumber ≥ ↑k
summary:
For every r ≥ 4 and k ≥ 2 is there some finite f(k,r) such that every graph of chromatic number ≥ f(k,r)
contains a subgraph of girth ≥ r and chromatic number ≥ k?

title: Erdos1082.erdos_1082.parts.i
statement: True ↔ ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))), EuclideanGeometry.NonTrilinear ↑A → A.card / 2 ≤ distinctDistances A
summary:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points with no three on a line.
Does $A$ determine at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ distinct distances?

title: Erdos1085.erdos_1085.variants.upper_d3
statement: True ↔ (fun n => ↑(Erdos1085.f 3 n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n ^ (4 / 3) * Real.log (Real.log ↑n)
summary: Is the $n^{4/3}\log\log n$ lower bound in 3D also an upper bound?.

title: Erdos1094.erdos_1094
statement: {(n, k) | 0 < k ∧ 2 * k ≤ n ∧ (n.choose k).minFac > max (n / k) k}.Finite
summary:
For all $n\ge 2k$ the least prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$ is $\le\max(n/k,k)$, with only
finitely many exceptions.

title: Erdos1095.erdos_1095.variants.log_isTheta
statement: (fun k => Real.log ↑(Erdos1095.g k)) =Θ[Filter.atTop] fun k => ↑k / Real.log ↑k
summary: Sorenson, Sorenson, and Webster [SSWE20] give heuristic evidence that $\log g(k) \asymp \frac{k}{\log k}$.

title: Erdos1095.erdos_1095.variants.lower_conjecture
statement: ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos1095.g k) ≥ Real.exp (c * ↑k / Real.log ↑k)
summary:
Erdős, Lacampagne, and Selfridge [ELS93] write 'it is clear to every right-thinking person' that
$g(k)\geq\exp(c\frac{k}{\log k})$ for some constant $c>0$.

title: Erdos11.erdos_11
statement: ∀ (n : ℕ), Odd n → 1 < n → ∃ k l, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l
summary: Is every odd $n > 1$ the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2?

title: Erdos1101.erdos_1101.parts.i
statement: True ↔ ∃ u, Erdos1101.IsGood u ∧ ∃ k, (fun n => ↑(u n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n ^ k
summary: 1. Is there a good sequence with polynomial growth?

title: Erdos1106.erdos_1106.parts.ii
statement: True ↔ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, Erdos1106.p i).primeFactors.card > n
summary:
Let $p(n)$ be the partition number of $n$ and $F(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of
$∏_{i= 1} ^ {n} p(n)$, $F(n)>n$ for sufficiently large $n$.

title: Erdos1107.erdos_1107
statement: ∀ r ≥ 2, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos1107.SumOfRPowerful r n
summary: Let $r \ge 2$. Is every large integer the sum of at most $r + 1$ many $r$-powerful numbers?

title: Erdos1108.erdos_1108.parts.i
statement: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 2, {a | a ∈ Erdos1108.FactorialSums ∧ ∃ m, m ^ k = a}.Finite
summary: For each $k \geq 2$, does the set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite sums of distinct factorials contain only finitely many $k$-th powers?

title: Erdos1113.erdos_1113.variants.filaseta_finch_kozek
statement: ∀ (k : ℕ), k.IsSierpinskiNumber → k.IsPerfectPower ∨ Erdos1113.HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k
summary:
**Filaseta–Finch–Kozek conjecture (2008).** Every Sierpiński number is either a perfect power
or possesses a finite covering set of primes.

title: Erdos1135.erdos_1135
statement: ∀ n > 0, ∃ m, CollatzConjecture.collatzStep^[m] n = 1
summary:
The Collatz conjecture states that for any positive integer $n$, there exists a natural
number $m$ such that the $m$-th term of the sequence is 1.

title: Erdos1137.erdos_1137
statement:
True ↔
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun x => ↑((Finset.range x).sup fun n => primeGap n * primeGap (n - 1)) / ↑((Finset.range x).sup primeGap) ^ 2)
    Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
summary:
Let $d_n=p_{n+1}-p_n$, where $p_n$ denotes the $n$th prime. Is it true that
$$\frac{\max_{n < x}d_{n}d_{n-1}}{(\max_{n < x}d_n)^2}\to 0$$ as $x\to \infty$?

title: Erdos1142.erdos_1142
statement: True ↔ Infinite ↑{n | Erdos1142.Erdos1142Prop n}
summary:
Are there infinitely many $n > 2$ such that $n - 2^k$ is prime for all $k \geq 1$ with $2^k < n$?

The only known such $n$ are $4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105$ (OEIS [A039669](https://oeis.org/A039669)).

title: Erdos1175.erdos_1175
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (κ : Cardinal.{u_1}),
    Cardinal.aleph0 < κ →
      ∃ μ,
        ∀ (V : Type u_1) (G : SimpleGraph V),
          G.chromaticCardinal = μ → ∃ H, H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = κ
summary:
Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable cardinal. Must there exist a cardinal $\lambda$ such that every
graph with chromatic number $\lambda$ contains a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number
$\kappa$?

Shelah proved that a negative answer is consistent when
$\kappa = \lambda = \aleph_1$ (see `erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency`).

title: Erdos1192.erdos_1192
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ r ≥ 2,
    ∃ A,
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos1192.f_r A r n > 0) ∧
        (fun x => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (x + 1), ↑(Erdos1192.f_r A r n) ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑x
summary:
Does there exist, for all $r\geq 2$, a basis $A$ of order $r$ (so that $f_r(n)>0$ for all
large $n$) such that $$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$ for all $x$?

title: Erdos120.erdos_120
statement: True ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℝ), A.Infinite → Erdos120.Erdos120For A
summary:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be an infinite set. Must there be a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
of positive measure which does not contain any set of the shape $a * A + b$
for some $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \neq 0$?

title: Erdos1203.erdos_1203
statement: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto Erdos1203.F Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary: Prove that $F(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.

title: Erdos1209.erdos_1209.parts.iii.d
statement: True ↔ ∃ n, {k | Squarefree (n + 2 ^ 2 ^ k)}.Infinite
summary: Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is infinitely often squarefree?

title: Erdos124.erdos124.ne_zero
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (k : ℕ),
    k ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (D : Finset ℕ),
        (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) →
          1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (↑d - 1)⁻¹ →
            D.gcd id = 1 → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, Erdos124.sumsOfDistinctPowers d k
summary:
Let $k \ne 0$ and $3\leq d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_r$ be integers of gcd equal to $1$ such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$
Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ is divisible by $d_i ^ k$ and has only the digits $0, 1$ when
written in base $d_i$?

Conjectured by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96]

title: Erdos126.erdos_126.variants.isLittleO
statement: ∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ), Erdos126.IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f → (fun n => ↑(f n)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n / Real.log ↑n
summary: Erdős says that $f(n) = o(\frac{n}{\log n})$ has never been proved.

title: Erdos128.erdos_128
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
    (∀ (V' : Set V),
        2 * V'.ncard + 1 ≥ Fintype.card V → 50 * (SimpleGraph.induce V' G).edgeSet.ncard > Fintype.card V ^ 2) →
      ¬G.CliqueFree 3
summary:
Let G be a graph with n vertices such that every induced subgraph on ≥ $n/2$
vertices has more than $n^2/50$ edges. Must G contain a triangle?

title: Erdos137.erdos_137.variants.multiple_powerful_factors
statement:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (m : ℕ),
      0 < m →
        ∃ P,
          P.card = k ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p ∧ p ∣ ∏ x ∈ Finset.Icc m (m + n), x ∧ ¬p ^ 2 ∣ ∏ x ∈ Finset.Icc m (m + n), x
summary:
Erdős [Er82c] conjectures that, if $k$ is fixed, then for all $n$ sufficiently large and all
positive integers $m$, there must be at least $k$ distinct primes $p$ such that
$p\mid m(m+1)\cdots (m+n)$ and yet $p^2$ does not divide the right hand side.

[Er82c] Erdős, Paul, "Miscellaneous problems in number theory". Congr. Numer. (1982), 25-45.,

title: Erdos138.erdos_138
statement: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑(Erdos138.W k) ^ (1 / ↑k)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
In [Er80] Erdős asks whether
$$ \lim_{k \to \infty} (W(k))^{1/k} = \infty $$

title: Erdos14.erdos_14.parts.i
statement: True ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), ∀ ε > 0, Erdos14.almostSquareRoot ε =O[Filter.atTop] Erdos14.nonUniqueSumCount A
summary:
Let $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$. Let $B ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ be the set of integers which are representable
in exactly one way as the sum of two elements from $A$. Is it true that for all
$\epsilon > 0$ and large $N$, $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| \gg_\epsilon N^{1/2 - \epsilon}$?

title: Erdos14.erdos_14.parts.ii
statement: True ↔ ∃ A, Erdos14.nonUniqueSumCount A =o[Filter.atTop] Erdos14.squareRoot
summary: Is it possible that $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| = o(N^\frac{1}{2})$?

title: Erdos141.erdos_141.variants.eleven
statement: True ↔ ∃ s, Erdos141.Set.IsAPAndPrimeProgressionOfLength s 11
summary: Are there $11$ consecutive primes in arithmetic progression?

title: Erdos142.erdos_142.variants.lower
statement: ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 < k → (fun N => ↑(Erdos142.r k N)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N / Real.log ↑N
summary:
Show that $r_k(N) = o_k(N / \log N)$, where $r_k(N)$ the largest possible size of a subset
of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ that does not contain any non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression.

title: Erdos143.erdos_143.parts.ii
statement: ∀ (A : Set ℝ), Erdos143.WellSeparatedSet A → Summable fun x => 1 / (↑x * Real.log ↑x)
summary:
Or
$$
\sum_{x \in A} \frac{1}{x \log x} < \infty,
$$

title: Erdos145.erdos_145
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ α ≥ 0,
    ∃ β,
      Filter.Tendsto (fun x => 1 / x * ∑ n ∈ Erdos145.A x, (↑(Erdos145.s (n + 1)) - ↑(Erdos145.s n)) ^ α) Filter.atTop
        (nhds β)
summary:
Let $s_1 < s_2 < \cdots$ be the sequence of squarefree numbers. Is it true that, for any
$\alpha\geq 0$,
$$
\lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{1}{x}\sum_{s_n\leq x}(s_{n+1}-s_n)^\alpha
$$
exists?

title: Erdos153.erdos_153
statement: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto Erdos153.f Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
Let $A$ be a finite Sidon set and $A+A=\{s_1<\cdots<s_t\}$. Is it true that
$$\frac{1}{t}\sum_{1\leq i<t}(s_{i+1}-s_i)^2 \to \infty$$
as $\lvert A\rvert\to \infty$?

title: Erdos155.erdos_155
statement: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos155.F (N + k) ≤ Erdos155.F N + 1
summary:
Is it true that for every $k \geq 1$ we have
$$
F(N + k) \leq F(N) + 1
$$
for all sufficiently large $N$?

title: Erdos156.erdos_156
statement: True ↔ (fun N => ↑(Erdos156.minMaximalSidonSet N)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N ^ (1 / 3)
summary:
Does there exist a maximal Sidon set $A\subset \{1,\ldots,N\}$ of size $O(N^{1/3})$?

A question of Erdős, Sárközy, and Sós [ESS94].

title: Erdos158.erdos_158
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.Infinite → Erdos158.B2 2 A → Filter.liminf (fun N => ↑(A ∩ Set.Iio N).ncard * ↑N ^ (-1 / 2)) Filter.atTop = 0
summary: Let `A` be an infinite `B₂[2]` set. Must `liminf |A ∩ {1, ..., N}| * N ^ (- 1 / 2) = 0`?

title: Erdos168.erdos_168.parts.ii
statement: True ↔ Irrational (Filter.limsup (fun N => ↑(Erdos168.F N) / ↑N) Filter.atTop)
summary: Is the limit $F(N)/N$ as $N \to \infty$ irrational?

title: Erdos17.erdos_17
statement: True ↔ {p | Erdos17.IsClusterPrime p}.Infinite
summary: **Erdős Problem 17.** Are there infinitely many cluster primes?

title: Erdos172.erdos_172
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (color : ℕ → Fin n) (m : ℕ),
    ∃ A, A.card ≥ m ∧ ∃ c, ∀ (S : Finset ↥A), S.Nonempty → color (∑ x ∈ S, ↑x) = c ∧ color (∏ x ∈ S, ↑x) = c
summary:
Is it true that in any finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exist arbitrarily large finite $A$ such that all sums
and products of distinct elements in $A$ are the same colour?

title: Erdos18.erdos_18b
statement: True ↔ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos18.practicalH n.factorial) < ↑n ^ ε
summary:
**Conjecture 2.**
Is it true that $h(n!) < n^{o(1)}$? That is, for all $\varepsilon > 0$,
is $h(n!) < n^\varepsilon$ for sufficiently large $n$?

title: Erdos184.erdos_184
statement:
∃ f,
  (f =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n) ∧
    ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ D, (∀ H ∈ D, Erdos184.IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧ Erdos184.IsDecomposition G D ∧ ↑D.card ≤ f (Fintype.card V)
summary: Any graph on $n$ vertices can be decomposed into $O(n)$ many edge-disjoint cycles and edges.

title: Erdos196.erdos_196
statement: True ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ ≃ ℕ), HasMonotoneAP (⇑f) 4
summary: Must every permutation of $\mathbb{N}$, contain a monotone 4-term arithmetic progression?

title: Erdos200.erdos_200
statement: True ↔ (fun n => ↑(Erdos200.longestPrimeArithmeticProgressions n)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => Real.log ↑n
summary: Does the longest arithmetic progression of primes in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ have length $o(\log N)$?

title: Erdos208.erdos_208.variants.log_bound
statement:
(fun n => ↑(Erdos208.erdos208.s (n + 1)) - ↑(Erdos208.erdos208.s n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n =>
  Real.log ↑(Erdos208.erdos208.s n)
summary:
In [Er79] Erdős says perhaps $s_{n+1} - s_n \ll \log s_n$, but he is 'very doubtful'.

[Er79] Erdős, Paul, __Some unconventional problems in number theory__. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.

title: Erdos212.erdos_212
statement: True ↔ ∃ u, Dense u ∧ u.Pairwise fun c₁ c₂ => dist c₁ c₂ ∈ Set.range Rat.cast
summary:
Is there a dense subset of ℝ^2 such that all pairwise distances
are rational?

title: Erdos213.erdos_213
statement: True ↔ ∀ n ≥ 4, Erdos213.Erdos213For n
summary:
Let $n \geq 4$. Are there $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no three on a line and no four on a circle,
such that all pairwise distances are integers?

title: Erdos218.erdos_218.variants.ge
statement: {n | primeGap (n + 1) ≤ primeGap n}.HasDensity (1 / 2)
summary:
The set of indices $n$ for which a prime gap is preceded by a larger or equal prime gap has a
natural density of $\frac 1 2$.

display_title: Erdős problem 218 - infinite equal prime gap
title: Erdos218.erdos_218.variants.infinite_equal_prime_gap
statement: {n | primeGap n = primeGap (n + 1)}.Infinite
summary:
There are infinitely many indices $n$ such that the prime gap at $n$ is equal to the prime gap
at $n+1$. This is equivalent to the existence of infinitely many arithmetic progressions of
length $3$, see `erdos_141.variants.infinite_three`.

title: Erdos218.erdos_218.variants.le
statement: {n | primeGap n ≤ primeGap (n + 1)}.HasDensity (1 / 2)
summary:
The set of indices $n$ for which a prime gap is followed by a larger or equal prime gap has a
natural density of $\frac 1 2$.

title: Erdos23.erdos_23
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V],
    Fintype.card V = 5 * n →
      ∀ (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ H ≤ G, H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ n ^ 2
summary: Can every triangle-free graph on $5n$ vertices be made bipartite by deleting at most $n^2$ edges?

title: Erdos233.erdos_233
statement: (fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, ↑(primeGap n) ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N * Real.log ↑N ^ 2
summary:
A conjecture by Heath-Brown:
The sum of squares of the first $N$ gaps between consecutive primes behaves like $N * (log N)^2$.

title: Erdos234.erdos_234
statement: True ↔ ∃ f, Continuous f ∧ ∀ (c : NNReal), {n | ↑(primeGap n) / Real.log ↑n < ↑c}.HasDensity (f c)
summary:
Is it true that for all `c ≥ 0`, the density `f c` of integers for which
`(p (n + 1) - p n) / log n < c` exists and is a continuous function of `c`?

title: Erdos236.erdos_236
statement: (fun n => ↑(Erdos236.f n)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => Real.log ↑n
summary: Let $f(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=p+2^k$ for prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$. Show that $f(n)=o(\log n)$.

title: Erdos238.erdos_238
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ c₁ > 0,
    ∀ c₂ > 0,
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop,
        ∃ k,
          c₁ * Real.log x < ↑k ∧
            ∃ f m,
              (∀ (i : Fin k), ↑(f i) ≤ x ∧ f i = Nat.nth Nat.Prime (m + ↑i)) ∧
                ∀ (i : Fin (k - 1)), c₂ < primeGap (m + ↑i)
summary:
Let `c₁, c₂ > 0`. Is it true that for any sufficiently large `x`, there exists more than
`c₁ * log x` many consecutive primes `≤ x` such that the difference between any two is `> c₂`?

title: Erdos241.erdos_241.variants.generalization
statement: ∀ r ≥ 2, Erdos241.BoseChowlaConjecture r
summary:
More generally, Bose and Chowla [BoCh62] conjectured that the maximum size of
$A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with all $r$-fold sums distinct (aside from the trivial coincidences)
then $\lvert A\rvert \sim N^{1/r}.$

title: Erdos242.erdos_242.variants.schinzel_generalization
statement: ∀ (a : ℕ), 0 < a → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ x y z, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < y ∧ y < z ∧ ↑a / ↑n = 1 / ↑x + 1 / ↑y + 1 / ↑z
summary:
Schinzel conjectured (see [Si56]) the generalisation that, for any fixed $a$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large in terms of $a$ then there exist distinct integers $1\leq x < y < z$ such that
$\frac{a}{n} = \frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z}.$

title: Erdos243.erdos_243
statement:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  StrictMono a →
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a n) / ↑(a (n - 1)) ^ 2) Filter.atTop (nhds 1) →
      (Summable fun x => 1 / ↑(a x)) → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, a n = a (n - 1) ^ 2 - a (n - 1) + 1
summary:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{a_{n-1}^2} = 1$ and $\sum \frac{1}{a_n} \in \mathbb{Q}$.

Then, for all sufficiently large $n \ge 1$, $a_n = a_{n-1}^2 - a_{n-1} + 1$.

title: Erdos244.erdos_244
statement: True ↔ ∀ C > 1, 0 < {x | ∃ p k, ∃ (_ : Nat.Prime p), p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ = x}.lowerDensity
summary:
Let $C > 1$. Does the set of integers of the form $p + \lfloor C^k \rfloor$,
for some prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$, have density $>0$?

title: Erdos247.erdos_247
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono n →
      Filter.limsup (fun k => ↑(n k) / ↑k.succ) Filter.atTop = ⊤ → Transcendental ℚ (∑' (k : ℕ), 1 / 2 ^ n k)
summary:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$$
  \limsup \frac{n_k}{k} = \infty.
$$
Is
$$
  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^{n_k}}
$$
transcendental?

title: Erdos249.erdos_249
statement: True ↔ Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ↑n.totient / 2 ^ n)
summary:
Is
$$\sum_{n} \frac{\phi(n)}{2^n}$$
irrational? Here $\phi$ is the Euler totient function.

title: Erdos25.erdos_25
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (seq_n : ℕ → ℕ) (seq_a : ℕ → ℤ),
    (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < seq_n i) →
      StrictMono seq_n → ∃ d, {x | ∀ (i : ℕ), ↑x < ↑(seq_n i) ∨ ¬↑x ≡ seq_a i [ZMOD ↑(seq_n i)]}.HasLogDensity d
summary:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an arbitrary sequence of integers, each with an associated residue class
$a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Let $A$ be the set of integers $n$ such that for every $i$ either $n < n_i$ or
$n \not\equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Must the logarithmic density of $A$ exist?

title: Erdos251.erdos_251
statement: True ↔ Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ↑(Nat.nth Nat.Prime n) / 2 ^ n)
summary: Is $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{p_n}{2^n}$ irrational? Here $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime ($p_1=2, p_2=3, \dots$).

title: Erdos252.erdos_252
statement: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, Irrational (Erdos252.erdos_252_sum k)
summary: Erdős Problem 252: irrationality of the sum for a given $k$.

title: Erdos257.erdos_257
statement: True ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite → Irrational (∑' (n : ↑A), 1 / (2 ^ ↑n - 1))
summary:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set. Is
$$
\sum_{n\in A} \frac{1}{2^n - 1}
$$
irrational?

title: Erdos263.erdos_263.parts.i
statement: True ↔ Erdos263.IsIrrationalitySequence fun n => 2 ^ 2 ^ n
summary: Is $a_n = 2^{2^n}$ an irrationality sequence in the above sense?

title: Erdos264.erdos_264.parts.ii
statement: True ↔ Erdos264.IsIrrationalitySequence Nat.factorial
summary: Is $n!$ an example of an irrationality sequence?

title: Erdos269.erdos_269.variants.irrational
statement: True ↔ ∀ (P : Finset ℕ), (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) → P.card ≥ 2 → Irrational (Erdos269.series ↑P)
summary:
Let $P$ be a finite set of primes with $|P| \ge 2$ and let
$\{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ be the set of positive integers whose prime factors
are all in $P$. Is the sum
$$ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{[a_1,\ldots,a_n]} $$
irrational?

title: Erdos272.erdos_272.variants.szabo_strong
statement: (fun N => ↑(Erdos272.maxArithInterCard N) - ↑N ^ 2 / 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N
summary:
Szabo asks whether the maximal $t$ is given by
$$
  \frac{N^2}{2} + O(N)
$$

title: Erdos274.herzog_schonheim
statement:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Group G],
  1 < ENat.card G →
    ∀ {ι : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Fintype ι],
      1 < Fintype.card ι →
        ∀ (P : Erdos274.Group.ExactCovering G ι), ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index
summary:
Let $G$ be a group, and let $A = \{a_1G_1, \dots, a_kG_k\}$ be a finite system of left cosets of
subgroups $G_1, \dots, G_k$ of $G$.

Herzog and Schönheim conjectured that if $A$ forms a partition of $G$ with $k > 1$, then the
indices $[G:G_1], \dots, [G:G_k]$ cannot be distinct.

title: Erdos28.erdos_28
statement: ∀ (A : Set ℕ), (A + A)ᶜ.Finite → Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep A n)) Filter.atTop = ⊤
summary:
If $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is such that $A + A$ contains all but finitely many integers then
$\limsup 1_A ∗ 1_A(n) = \infty$.

title: Erdos282.erdos_282
statement: ∀ {x : ℚ}, x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 → Odd x.den → Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem {n | Odd n} x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0
summary:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set and consider the following
greedy algorithm for a rational $x\in (0,1)$: choose the minimal $n\in A$ such
that $n\geq 1/x$ and repeat with $x$ replaced by $x-\frac{1}{n}$. If this
terminates after finitely many steps then this produces a representation of
$x$ as the sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators from $A$.

Does this process always terminate if $x$ has odd denominator and $A$ is the
set of odd numbers?

title: Erdos287.erdos_287
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, ⋯⟩ → ∑ i, 1 / ↑(s i) = 1 → 3 ≤ Erdos287.max_gap k s
summary:
Let $k\geq2$. Is it true that, for any distinct integers
$1 < n_1 < \cdots < n_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{n_i} = 1$,
we must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$?

title: Erdos291.erdos_291.parts.i
statement: True ↔ {n | (Erdos291.a n).gcd (Erdos291.L n) = 1}.Infinite
summary:
Let $n\geq 1$ and define $L_n$ to be the least common multiple of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $a_n$ by
$\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{1}{k}=\frac{a_n}{L_n}$.

Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)=1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?

display_title: Erdős problem 291 - shiu heuristic density zero
title: Erdos291.erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_density_zero
statement: Filter.Tendsto (fun N => ↑{n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N | (Erdos291.a n).gcd (Erdos291.L n) = 1}.card / ↑N) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
summary:
In particular, there should be infinitely many $n$, but the set of such $n$ should have
density zero. Unfortunately this heuristic is difficult to turn into a proof.

title: Erdos3.erdos_3
statement: True ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), (¬Summable fun a => 1 / ↑↑a) → ∃ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S ⊆ A, S.IsAPOfLength ↑k
summary:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has $\sum_{n \in A}\frac 1 n = \infty$, then must $A$ contain arbitrarily
long arithmetic progressions?

title: Erdos30.erdos_30
statement: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, (fun N => ↑(Erdos30.h N) - √↑N) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N ^ ε
summary: Is it true that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $h(N) = \sqrt N + O_{\varepsilon}(N^\varepsilon)$

title: Erdos304.upper_bound
statement: True ↔ (fun b => ↑(Erdos304.smallestCollectionTo b)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun b => Real.log (Real.log ↑b)
summary: Is it true that $$N(b) \ll \log \log b$$?

title: Erdos307.erdos_307
statement: True ↔ ∃ P Q, (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) ∧ (∀ q ∈ Q, Nat.Prime q) ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (↑p)⁻¹) * ∑ q ∈ Q, (↑q)⁻¹
summary:
Are there two finite set of primes $P$ and $Q$ such that

$$
1 = \left( \sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} \right) \left( \sum_{q \in Q} \frac{1}{q} \right)
$$
?

Asked by Barbeau [Ba76].

[Ba76] Barbeau, E. J., _Computer challenge corner: Problem 477: A brute force program._

display_title: Erdős problem 313 - primary pseudoperfect are infinite
title: Erdos313.erdos_313.variants.primary_pseudoperfect_are_infinite
statement: {n | Erdos313.IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n}.Infinite
summary: It is conjectured that the set of primary pseudoperfect numbers is infinite.

title: Erdos317.erdos_317.variants.claim2
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (δ : Fin n → ℚ),
      δ '' Set.univ ⊆ {-1, 0, 1} → |∑ k, δ k / (↑↑k + 1)| ≠ 0 → |∑ k, δ k / (↑↑k + 1)| > 1 / ↑((Finset.Icc 1 n).lcm id)
summary:
Is it true that for sufficiently large $n$, for any $\delta_k\in \{-1,0,1\}$,
$$\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{\delta_k}{k}\right\rvert > \frac{1}{[1,\ldots,n]}$$
whenever the left-hand side is not zero?

title: Erdos32.erdos_32
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ A,
    Erdos32.IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A ∧
      (fun N => ↑{x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N | x ∈ A}.card) =o[Filter.atTop] fun N => Real.log ↑N ^ 2
summary:
Does there exist a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| = o((\log N)^2)$
and every sufficiently large integer can be written as $p + a$ for some prime $p$ and $a \in A$?

title: Erdos323.erdos_323.parts.i
statement: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ ε > 0, (fun x => ↑x ^ (1 - ε)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑(Erdos323.f k k x)
summary:
Is it true that $f_{k,k}(x) \gg_\epsilon x^{1-\epsilon}$ for all $\epsilon>0$?

This would have significant applications to Waring's problem. Erdős and Graham describe this as
'unattackable by the methods at our disposal'.

title: Erdos323.erdos_323.parts.ii
statement: True ↔ ∀ (k m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → m < k → (fun x => ↑x ^ (↑m / ↑k)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑(Erdos323.f k m x)
summary: Is it true that if $m < k$ then $f_{k,m}(x) \gg x^{m/k}$ for sufficiently large $x$?

title: Erdos323.erdos_323.variants.k_gt_2
statement: True ↔ ∀ k > 2, (fun x => ↑(Erdos323.f k k x)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑x
summary: For $k>2$ it is not known if $f_{k,k}(x)=o(x)$.

title: Erdos324.erdos_324.variants.quintic
statement:
Set.InjOn
  (fun x =>
    match x with
    | (a, b) => a ^ 5 + b ^ 5)
  {(a, b) | a < b}
summary:
Probably $f(x) = x^5$ has the property that the sums $f(a)+f(b)$ with
$a < b$ nonnegative integers are distinct.

title: Erdos325.erdos_325
statement: True ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → (fun x => ↑x ^ (3 / ↑k)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑(Erdos325.cardIsSumThreePowerBelow k x)
summary:
Writing $f_{k, 3}(x)$ for the number of integers $\leq x$ which are the sum of three $k$th powers,
is it true that $f_{k, 3}(x) \gg x ^ (3 / k)$?

title: Erdos340.erdos_340
statement: ∀ ε > 0, (fun n => √↑n / ↑n ^ ε) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(Set.range Finset.greedySidon ∩ Set.Icc 1 n).ncard
summary:
Let $A = \{1, 2, 4, 8, 13, 21, 31, 45, 66, 81, 97, \ldots\}$ be the greedy Sidon sequence:
we begin with $1$ and iteratively include the next smallest integer that preserves the
Sidon property (i.e. there are no non-trivial solutions to $a + b = c + d$). What is the
order of growth of $A$? Is it true that $|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| \gg N^{1/2 - \varepsilon}$
for all $\varepsilon > 0$ and large $N$?

display_title: Erdős problem 340 - sub has Pos Density
title: Erdos340.erdos_340.variants.sub_hasPosDensity
statement: (Set.range Finset.greedySidon - Set.range Finset.greedySidon).HasPosDensity
summary:
Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] also asked about the difference set $A - A$ and whether this has
positive density.

[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).

title: Erdos354.erdos_354.parts.i
statement: True ↔ ∀ α > 0, ∀ β > 0, Irrational (α / β) → IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (Erdos354.FloorMultiples.interleave α β 2)
summary:
Let $\alpha,\beta\in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that $\alpha/\beta$ is irrational. Is the multiset
$$\{ \lfloor \alpha\rfloor,\lfloor 2\alpha\rfloor,\lfloor 4\alpha\rfloor,\ldots\}\cup
\{ \lfloor \beta\rfloor,\lfloor 2\beta\rfloor,\lfloor 4\beta\rfloor,\ldots\}$$ complete?

title: Erdos357.erdos_357.parts.i
statement: (fun n => ↑(Erdos357.f n)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n
summary:
Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct. Is $f(n)=o(n)$?

title: Erdos357.erdos_357.variants.infinite_set_density
statement: ∀ (A : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono A → Erdos357.HasDistinctSums A → (Set.range A).HasDensity 0
summary:
Suppose $A$ is an infinite set such that all finite sums of consecutive terms of $A$ are distinct.
Then it is conjectured that $A$ has density 0.

title: Erdos357.erdos_357.variants.infinite_set_sum
statement: ∀ (A : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono A → Erdos357.HasDistinctSums A → Summable fun i => 1 / ↑(A i)
summary:
Suppose $A$ is an infinite set such that all finite sums of consecutive terms of $A$ are distinct.
Then it is conjectured that the sum $\sum_k \frac{1}{a_k}$ converges.

title: Erdos357.erdos_357.variants.monotone.parts.i
statement: (fun n => ↑(Erdos357.h n)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n
summary:
Let $h(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 \leq \dotsc \leq a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct. Is $h(n)=o(n)$?

title: Erdos359.erdos_359.parts.i
statement: ∀ (A : ℕ → ℕ), Erdos359.IsGoodFor A 1 → Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑(A k) / ↑k) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
Let $a_1< a_2 < ⋯ $ be an infinite sequence of integers such that $a_1=1$ and $a_{i+1}$ is the
least integer which is not a sum of consecutive earlier $a_j$s. Show that $a_k / k \to \infty$.

title: Erdos359.erdos_359.parts.ii
statement:
∀ (A : ℕ → ℕ),
  Erdos359.IsGoodFor A 1 → ∀ (c : ℝ), 0 < c → Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑(A k) / ↑k ^ (1 + c)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
summary:
Let $a_1< a_2 < ⋯ $ be an infinite sequence of integers such that $a_1=1$ and $a_{i+1}$ is the
least integer which is not a sum of consecutive earlier $a_j$s. Show that $a_k / k ^ {1 + c} \to 0$
for any $c > 0$.

display_title: Erdős problem 359 - is Good For 1 asymptotic
title: Erdos359.erdos_359.variants.isGoodFor_1_asymptotic
statement:
∀ (A : ℕ → ℕ),
  Erdos359.IsGoodFor A 1 →
    Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun k => ↑(A k)) fun k => ↑k * Real.log ↑k / Real.log (Real.log ↑k)
summary:
Suppose monotone sequence $A$ satisfies the following: `A 0 = 1` and for all `j`, `A (j + 1)` is the
smallest natural number that cannot be written as a sum of consecutive terms of `A 0, ..., A j`.
Then it is conjectured that $$a_k ~ \frac{k \log k}{\log \log k}$$.

title: Erdos364.erdos_364
statement: ¬∃ n, n.Powerful ∧ (n + 1).Powerful ∧ (n + 2).Powerful
summary: There is no consecutive triple of powerful numbers.

title: Erdos364.erdos_364.variants.strong
statement:
∃ c,
  ∃ (_ : c > 0), ∀ (k : ℕ), ↑(Nat.nth Nat.Powerful (k + 2)) - ↑(Nat.nth Nat.Powerful k) > ↑(Nat.nth Nat.Powerful k) ^ c
summary:
Erdős [Er76d] conjectured a stronger statement: if $n_k$ is the $k$th powerful number,
then $n_{k+2} - n_k > n_k^c$ for some constant $c > 0$.

[Er76d] Erdős, P., Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.

title: Erdos366.erdos_366
statement: True ↔ ∃ n > 0, Nat.Full 2 n ∧ Nat.Full 3 (n + 1)
summary: Are there any $2$-full $n$ such that $n+1$ is $3$-full?

title: Erdos371.erdos_371
statement: {n | (n + 1).maxPrimeFac > n.maxPrimeFac}.HasDensity (1 / 2)
summary:
Let $P(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$. Show that the set of $n$
with $P(n+1) > P(n)$ has density $\frac{1}{2}$.

title: Erdos373.erdos_373
statement: Erdos373.S.Finite
summary:
Show that the equation `n!=a_1!a_2!···a_k!`, with `n−1 > a_1 ≥ a_2 ≥ ··· ≥ a_k`, has
only finitely many solutions.

title: Erdos373.erdos_373.variants.maximal_solution
summary:
Hickerson conjectured the largest solution the equation `n!=a_1!a_2!···a_k!`, with
`n−1 > a_1 ≥ a_2 ≥ ··· ≥ a_k`, is `16!=14!5!2!`.

title: Erdos373.erdos_373.variants.suranyi
statement: {(n, a, b) | n.factorial = a.factorial * b.factorial ∧ 1 < n ∧ 1 < a ∧ 1 < b ∧ b ≤ a ∧ a + 1 ≠ n} = {(10, 7, 6)}
summary:
Surányi was the first to conjecture that the only non-trivial solution to `a!b!=n!`
is `6!7!=10!`.

title: Erdos375.erdos_375
statement: True ↔ Erdos375.Erdos375Prop
summary: Is `Erdos375Prop` true?

title: Erdos376.erdos_376
statement: True ↔ {n | n.centralBinom.Coprime 105}.Infinite
summary: Are there infinitely many $n$ such that ${2n\choose n}$ is coprime to $105$?

title: Erdos383.erdos_383
statement: True ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), {p | Nat.Prime p ∧ (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 0 k, (p ^ 2 + i)).maxPrimeFac = p}.Infinite
summary:
Is it true that for every $k$ there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that the largest prime
divisor of
$$
  \prod_{i = 0}^k (p ^ 2 + i)
$$
is $p$?

title: Erdos385.erdos_385.parts.i
statement: True ↔ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, n < Erdos385.F n
summary:
Let $F(n) := \max\{m + p(m) \mid  \textrm{$m < n$ composite}\}\}$ where $p(m)$ is the least
prime divisor of $m$. Is it true that $F(n)>n$ for all sufficiently large $n$?

title: Erdos386.erdos_386.variants.two
statement: True ↔ ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 2 ≤ n - 2 ∧ ∃ p q, n.choose 2 = ∏ i ∈ Finset.Ico p q, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i
summary: Can $\binom{n}{2}$ be the product of consecutive primes infinitely often?

title: Erdos39.erdos_39
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ A, A.Infinite ∧ IsSidon A ∧ ∀ ε > 0, (fun x => ↑x ^ (1 / 2 - ε)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑(Set.Icc 1 N ∩ A).ncard
summary:
Is there an infinite Sidon set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ such that
$\lvert A\cap \{1\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg_\epsilon N^{1/2-\epsilon}$
for all $\varepsilon > 0$?

title: Erdos396.erdos_396
statement: True ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), ∃ n, n.descFactorial (k + 1) ∣ n.centralBinom
summary:
Is it true that for every $k$ there exists $n$ such that
$$\prod_{0\leq i\leq k}(n-i) \mid \binom{2n}{n}?$$

title: Erdos400.erdos_400.parts.i
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 2,
    ∃ c,
      Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun x => ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 x, ↑(Erdos400.g k n)) fun x =>
        c * ↑x * Real.log ↑x
summary: Can one show that $\sum_{n\leq x}g_k(n) \sim c_k x\log x$ for some constant $c_k$?

title: Erdos406.erdos_406.variants.one_two
statement: IsGreatest {n | n.isPowerOfTwo ∧ Nat.digits 3 n ⊆ [1, 2]} (2 ^ 15)
summary:
If we only allow the digits $1$ and $2$ then $2^{15}$ seems to be the largest such power
of $2$.

title: Erdos409.erdos_409.variants.sigma_termination
statement: ∀ n > 1, ∃ i, Nat.Prime ((fun x => (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) x - 1)^[i] n)
summary:
If $n > 1$ then the iteration $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ necessarily reaches a prime.
Note: this is open — it is not clear that the σ iteration always terminates,
since it is non-decreasing (unlike the φ iteration which is strictly decreasing).

title: Erdos41.erdos_41
statement:
∀ (A : Set ℕ),
  Erdos41.NtupleCondition A 3 →
    A.Infinite → Filter.liminf (fun N => ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard / ↑N ^ (1 / 3)) Filter.atTop = 0
summary:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that the triple sums $a+b+c$ are all distinct
for $a,b,c \in A$ (aside from the trivial coincidences). Is it true that
$$\liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{\lvert A \cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}{N^{1/3}}=0?$$

title: Erdos410.erdos_410
statement: True ↔ ∀ n > 1, Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑((⇑(ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1))^[k] n) ^ (1 / ↑k)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
Let $σ_1(n) = σ(n)$, the sum of divisors function, and $σ_k(n) = σ(σ_{k-1}(n))$.

Is it true that $\lim_{k → ∞} σ_k(n)^{\frac 1 k} = ∞$?

This is problem (iii) from
Erdos, Granville, Pomerance, Spiro
"On the normal behavior of the iterates of some arithmetical functions"
(page 169 of the book "Analytic Number Theory", 1990).

title: Erdos412.erdos_412
statement: True ↔ ∀ m ≥ 2, ∀ n ≥ 2, ∃ i j, (⇑(ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1))^[i] m = (⇑(ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1))^[j] n
summary:
Let $σ_1(n)=σ(n)$, the sum of divisors function, and $σ_k(n) = σ(σ_{k-1}(n))$.
Is it true that, for every $m, n ≥ 2$, there exist some $i, j$ such that $σ_i(m) = σ_j(n)$?

title: Erdos413.erdos_413.parts.i
statement: True ↔ {n | Erdos413.IsBarrier (fun m => ↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors m)) n}.Infinite
summary: Are there infinitely many barriers for `ω`?

title: Erdos414.erdos_414
statement: True ↔ ∀ m > 0, ∀ n > 0, ∃ i j, Erdos414.h^[i] m = Erdos414.h^[j] n
summary:
Let $h_1(n) = h(n)$ and $h_k(n) = h(h_{k-1}(n))$. Is it true, for any $m,n$, there exist
$i$ and $j$ such that $h_i(m) = h_j(n)$?

title: Erdos416.erdos_416.parts.i
statement: Filter.Tendsto (fun x => Erdos416.V (2 * x) / Erdos416.V x) Filter.atTop (nhds 2)
summary: Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable. Does `V(2x)/V(x)→2` ?

title: Erdos428.erdos_428
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ A,
    (∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a → a < n → Nat.Prime (n - a)) ∧
      Filter.liminf (fun n => Erdos428.primeDensityRatio A n) Filter.atTop > 0
summary:
Is there a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that, for infinitely many $n$, all of $n-a$
are prime for all $a\in A$ with $0 < a < n$ and $$\liminf\frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{\pi(x)}>0?$$

title: Erdos44.erdos_44
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ N ≥ 1,
    ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      IsSidon ↑A → ∀ ε > 0, ∃ M > N, ∃ B ⊆ Finset.Icc (N + 1) M, IsSidon (↑A ∪ ↑B) ∧ (1 - ε) * √↑M ≤ ↑(A ∪ B).card
summary:
**Erdős Problem 44:** Let N ≥ 1 and `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` be a Sidon set. Is it true that, for any ε > 0,
there exist M = M(ε) and `B ⊆ {N+1,…,M}` such that `A ∪ B ⊆ {1,…,M}` is a Sidon set
of size at least `(1−ε)M^{1/2}`?

This problem asks whether any Sidon set can be extended to achieve a density
arbitrarily close to the optimal density for Sidon sets.

title: Erdos445.erdos_445
statement: True ↔ ∀ c > 1 / 2, ∀ᶠ (p : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Nat.Prime p → ∀ (n : ℕ), Erdos445.Erdos445Prop c p n
summary:
Is it true that, for any $c>1/2$, if $p$ is a sufficiently large prime then, for any
$n\geq 0$, there exist $a,b\in(n,n+p^c)$ such that $ab\equiv 1\pmod{p}$?

This is discussed in this MathOverflow question [MathOverflow].

title: Erdos454.erdos_454
statement: True ↔ Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑(Erdos454.f n) - 2 * ↑(Nat.nth Prime n)) Filter.atTop = ⊤
summary: Is it true that `limsup (fun n => (f n - 2 * n.nth Prime : ℕ∞)) atTop = ⊤`?

title: Erdos455.erdos_455
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (q : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono q →
      (∀ (n : ℕ), Nat.Prime (q n) ∧ q (n + 2) - q (n + 1) ≥ q (n + 1) - q n) →
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(q n) / ↑n ^ 2) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
Let `q : ℕ → ℕ` be a strictly increasing sequence of primes such that
`q (n + 2) - q (n + 1) ≥ q (n + 1) - q n`. Must `lim q n / (n ^ 2) = ∞`?

title: Erdos456.erdos_456.parts.iii
statement: True ↔ {q | Nat.Prime q ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), Erdos456.m n = q ↔ n = q - 1}.Infinite
summary: Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p-1$ is the only $n$ for which $m_n=p$?

title: Erdos458.erdos_458
statement: True ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), Erdos458.lcm_upto (Nat.nth Prime (k + 1) - 1) < Nat.nth Prime k * Erdos458.lcm_upto (Nat.nth Prime k)
summary:
Let $\operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, n)$ denote the least common multiple of $\{1, \dots, n\}$.
Let $p_k$ be the $k$-th prime.
Is it true that for all $k \geq 1$, $\operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, p_{k+1}-1) < p_k \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, p_k)$?

title: Erdos463.erdos_463
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ f,
    ∃ (_ : Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop Filter.atTop),
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ m, m.Composite ∧ n + f n < m ∧ m < n + m.minFac
summary:
Is there a function $f$ with $f(n)\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ such that,
for all large $n$, there is a composite number $m$ such that
$$
n + f(n) < m < n + p(m)
$$
Here $p(m)$ is the least prime factor of $m$.

title: Erdos479.erdos_479
statement: True ↔ ∀ (k k : ℤ), k ≠ 1 → {n | 2 ^ n ≡ k [ZMOD ↑n]}.Infinite
summary:
Is it true that, for every integer $k\neq 1$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$2^n\equiv k\pmod{n}$?

title: Erdos495.erdos_495
statement: True ↔ ∀ (α β : ℝ), Filter.liminf (fun n => ↑n * distToNearestInt (↑n * α) * distToNearestInt (↑n * β)) Filter.atTop = 0
summary:
Let $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb{R}$. Is it true that$$\liminf_{n\to \infty} n \| n\alpha \|
\| n\beta\| =0$$? This is also known as the Littlewood conjecture.

title: Erdos50.erdos_50
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (f : ℝ → ℝ), Erdos50.IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f → ¬∃ x ∈ Set.Icc 0 1, ∃ y > 0, HasDerivWithinAt f y (Set.Icc 0 1) x
summary:
Let $f$ be the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$, so that for each $c \in [0,1]$,
$f(c)$ is the natural density of $\{n : \varphi(n) < cn\}$. Is it true that there is no $x$ such
that the derivative $f'(x)$ exists and is positive?

title: Erdos51.erdos_51
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ A n,
    A.Infinite ∧
      (∀ (a : ↑A), IsLeast (Nat.totient ⁻¹' {↑a}) (n a)) ∧
        Filter.Tendsto (fun a => ↑(n a) / ↑↑a) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
Is there an infinite set $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $a \in A$,
there is an integer n such that $\phi(n)=a$, and
yet if $n_a$ is the smallest such integer, then $\frac{n_a}{a} → \infty$ as $a → ∞$?

title: Erdos517.erdos_517
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ {f : ℂ → ℂ} {n : ℕ → ℕ},
    HasFabryGaps n →
      ∀ {a : ℕ → ℂ},
        (∀ (k : ℕ), a k ≠ 0) → (∀ (z : ℂ), HasSum (fun k => a k * z ^ n k) (f z)) → ∀ (z : ℂ), {x | f x = z}.Infinite
summary:
If `f(z) = ∑ aₖzⁿₖ` is an entire function (with `aₖ ≠ 0` for all `k`) such that `nₖ / k → ∞`,
is it true that `f` assumes every value infinitely often?

title: Erdos52.erdos_52
statement: True ↔ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (A : Finset ℤ), max ↑(A + A).card ↑(A * A).card ≥ C * ↑A.card ^ (2 - ε)
summary:
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$
$\max( \lvert A+A\rvert,\lvert AA\rvert)\gg_\epsilon \lvert A\rvert^{2-\epsilon}?$

title: Erdos535.erdos_535
statement: ∀ r ≥ 3, ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos535.f r N) ≤ ↑N ^ (c / Real.log (Real.log ↑N))
summary:
Let $r \geq 3$, and let $f_r(N)$ denote the size of the largest subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$
such that no subset of size $r$ has the same pairwise greatest common divisor between all
elements. Erdős [Er64] proved that $f_3(N) > N^{c/\log\log N}$ for some constant $c > 0$, and
conjectured this should also be an upper bound; here we state the conjectural upper bound
for all $r \geq 3$.

See also [536].

title: Erdos535.erdos_535.variants.first_open_case
statement: ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos535.f 3 N) ≤ ↑N ^ (c / Real.log (Real.log ↑N))
summary:
The first open case of Erdős Problem 535 is $r = 3$: there should exist $c > 0$ such that
$f_3(N) \leq N^{c/\log\log N}$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Erdos564.erdos_564
statement: True ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 2 ^ 2 ^ (c * n) ≤ ↑(Combinatorics.hypergraphRamsey 3 n)
summary:
Let $R_3(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that if the edges of the $3$-uniform hypergraph on $m$
vertices are $2$-coloured then there is a monochromatic copy of the complete $3$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

Is there some constant $c>0$ such that
$$ R_3(n) \geq 2^{2^{cn}}? $$

title: Erdos579.erdos_579
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (δ : ℝ),
    0 < δ →
      ∃ c,
        0 < c ∧
          ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
            ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
              Erdos579.octahedron.Free G → δ * ↑n ^ 2 ≤ ↑G.edgeFinset.card → c * ↑n ≤ ↑G.indepNum
summary:
Let $\delta > 0$. If $n$ is sufficiently large and $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with no
$K_{2,2,2}$ (the octahedron) and at least $\delta n^2$ edges, must $G$ contain an independent
set of size $\gg_\delta n$?

This is a problem of Erdős, Hajnal, Sós, and Szemerédi [EHSS83]. It is **open**; they proved
the statement for $\delta > 1/8$ (see `erdos_579.variants.ehss_large_delta`), and the
difficulty is to push the edge-density threshold down to an arbitrary $\delta > 0$.

Here $K_{2,2,2}$ is the complete tripartite graph with all parts of size $2$, encoded as
`completeMultipartiteGraph (fun _ : Fin 3 => Fin 2)`; "contains no $K_{2,2,2}$" is expressed
via `SimpleGraph.Free`.

title: Erdos600.erdos_600.parts.i
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (r : ℕ),
    2 ≤ r →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos600.eFunction n (r + 1)) - ↑(Erdos600.eFunction n r)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary: Let $r \geq 2$. Is it true that $e(n,r+1) - e(n,r) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$?

title: Erdos61.erdos_61
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] [inst_1 : DecidableEq α] (H : SimpleGraph α),
    ∃ c > 0, Erdos61.IsErdosHajnalLowerBound H fun n => ↑n ^ c
summary:
The Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture states that there is a constant $c(H) > 0$ for each
$H$ such that we can take $f(n) = n^{c(H)}$ in the above formulation.

title: Erdos617.erdos_617
statement:
∀ r ≥ 3,
  ∀ {V : Type} [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V],
    Fintype.card V = r ^ 2 + 1 →
      ∀ (coloring : Sym2 V → Fin r), ∃ S k, S.card = r + 1 ∧ ∀ u ∈ S, ∀ v ∈ S, u ≠ v → coloring s(u, v) ≠ k
summary:
Let $r\geq 3$. If the edges of $K_{r^2+1}$ are $r$-coloured then there exist $r+1$ vertices with at
least one colour missing on the edges of the induced $K_{r+1}$.

In other words, there is no balanced colouring.

A conjecture of Erdős and Gyárfás [ErGy99].

title: Erdos624.erdos_624
statement: Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos624.H n) - Real.logb 2 ↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
Let $X$ be a finite set of size $n$ and $H(n)$ be such that there is a function
$f:\{A : A\subseteq X\}\to X$ so that for every $Y\subseteq X$ with $\lvert Y\rvert \geq H(n)$
we have $\left\{ f(A) : A\subseteq Y\right\}=X$.
Prove that $H(n)-\log_2 n \to \infty$.

title: Erdos647.erdos_647
statement: True ↔ ∃ n > 24, ⨆ m, ↑m + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 0) ↑m ≤ n + 2
summary:
Let $\tau(n)$ count the number of divisors of $n$. Is there some $n > 24$ such that
$$
  \max_{m < n}(m + \tau(m)) \leq n + 2?
$$

title: Erdos653.erdos_653
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ o,
    o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (1 - o n) * ↑n ≤ ↑(EuclideanGeometry.maximalDistinctDistancesFrom n)
summary:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $R(x_i)=\#\{ \lvert x_j-x_i\rvert : j\neq i\}$,
where the points are ordered such that
$$R(x_1)\leq \cdots \leq R(x_n).$$
Let $g(n)$ be the maximum number of distinct values the $R(x_i)$ can take. Is it true that
$g(n) \geq (1-o(1))n$?

title: Erdos66.erdos_66
statement: True ↔ ∃ A c, c ≠ 0 ∧ Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep A n) / Real.log ↑n) Filter.atTop (nhds c)
summary:
Is there and $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ is such that
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{1_A\ast 1_A(n)}{\log n}$$
exists and is $\ne 0$?

title: Erdos672.erdos_672
statement: True ↔ ∀ (k l : ℕ), l > 1 → k ≥ 4 → Erdos672.Erdos672With k l
summary:
Can the product of an arithmetic progression of positive integers $n, n + d, ..., n + (k - 1)d$
of length ≥ 4, with $(n, d) = 1$, be a perfect power?

title: Erdos677.erdos_677
statement: ∀ (m n k : ℕ), k > 0 → m ≥ n + k → Finset.lcmInterval m k ≠ Finset.lcmInterval n k
summary:
Denote by $M(n, k)$ the least common multiple of the finite set $\{n+1, \dotsc, n+k\}$.
Is it true that for all $m \geq n + k$, we get $M(m, k) \neq M(n, k)$?

title: Erdos68.erdos_68
statement: True ↔ Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), 1 / (↑(n + 2).factorial - 1))
summary:
Is
$$\sum_{n=2}^\infty \frac{1}{n!-1}$$
irrational?

title: Erdos680.erdos_680.parts.i
statement: True ↔ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ k, k ≠ 0 ∧ (n + k).minFac > k ^ 2 + 1
summary:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists some $k$ such that
$$
p(n+k)>k^2+1,
$$
where $p(m)$ denotes the least prime factor of $m$?

title: Erdos680.erdos_680.parts.ii
statement: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∃ C > 0, ¬∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ k, k ≠ 0 ∧ ↑(n + k).minFac > Real.exp ((1 + ε) * √↑k) + C
summary:
Can one prove this is false if we replace $k^2+1$ by $e^{(1+\epsilon)\sqrt{k}}+C_\epsilon$, for all
$\epsilon>0$, where $C_\epsilon>0$ is some constant?

title: Erdos681.erdos_681
statement: True ↔ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ k > 0, (n + k).Composite ∧ ∀ (p : ℕ), Erdos681.IsLPF p (n + k) → p > k ^ 2
summary:
**Erdős problem 681.**
Is it true that for all large $n$ there exists $k$
such that $n + k$ is composite and $p(n+k) > k^2$,
where $p(m)$ is the least prime factor of $m$ ?

title: Erdos686.erdos_686.variants.four
statement: True ↔ ∃ k ≥ 2, ∃ n, ∃ m ≥ n + k, 4 = ↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / ↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))
summary:
Can $4$ be written as
$$4=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?

title: Erdos686.erdos_686.variants.twenty_five
statement: True ↔ ∃ k ≥ 2, ∃ n, ∃ m ≥ n + k, 25 = ↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / ↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))
summary:
Can $25$ be written as
$$25=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?

title: Erdos688.erdos_688.parts.ii
statement: True ↔ Erdos688.epsilonFunction =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => 1
summary: In particular, is it true that $\epsilon_n = o(1)$?

title: Erdos695.erdos_695
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ {q : ℕ → ℕ},
    StrictMono q →
      (∀ (i : ℕ), Nat.Prime (q i)) →
        (∀ (i : ℕ), q (i + 1) % q i = 1) → Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑(q k) ^ (1 / ↑k)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
Let $q_1 < q_2 < \cdots$ be a sequence of primes such that $q_{i + 1} \equiv 1 \pmod{q_i}$. Is it
true that
$$
\lim_{k \to \infty} q_k^{1/k} = \infty?
$$

title: Erdos695.erdos_695.variants.upperBound
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ q,
    StrictMono q ∧
      (∀ (i : ℕ), Nat.Prime (q i)) ∧
        (∀ (i : ℕ), q (i + 1) % q i = 1) ∧
          ∃ o, o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ), ↑(q k) ≤ Real.exp ((↑k + 1) * Real.log (↑k + 1) ^ (1 + o k))
summary:
Is there a sequence of primes $q_1 < q_2 < \cdots$ such that $q_{i + 1} \equiv 1 \pmod{q_i}$ and
$$
q(k) \leq \exp(k (\log k)^{1 + o(1)})?
$$

title: Erdos699.erdos_699
statement: True ↔ ∀ (n i j : ℕ), 1 ≤ i → i < j → j ≤ n / 2 → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ i ≤ p ∧ p ∣ (n.choose i).gcd (n.choose j)
summary:
**Erdős Problem 699.** Is it true that for every $1 \le i < j \le n / 2$ there exists a prime
$p \ge i$ with $p \mid \gcd\big(\binom{n}{i}, \binom{n}{j}\big)$?

display_title: Erdős problem 70 - omega times two four
title: Erdos70.erdos_70.variants.omega_times_two_four
statement: True ↔ Erdos70.OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 Cardinal.continuum.ord (Ordinal.omega0 * 2) 4
summary:
**First open case beyond Erdős–Rado**: $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega \cdot 2, 4)^3_2$.

Erdős and Rado proved $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega + n, 4)^3_2$ for every finite $n \ge 2$
(see `erdos_rado`), which covers all red ordinals below $\omega \cdot 2 = \omega + \omega$.
This variant asks whether the result extends to $\beta = \omega \cdot 2$, the simplest
countable ordinal not covered by their theorem.

title: Erdos701.erdos_701
summary:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of sets closed under taking subsets (i.e. if
$B\subseteq A\in\mathcal{F}$ then $B\in \mathcal{F}$). There exists some element $x$ such that
whenever $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq \mathcal{F}$ is an intersecting subfamily we have
$$\lvert \mathcal{F}'\rvert \leq \lvert \{ A\in \mathcal{F} : x\in A\}\rvert.$$

title: Erdos723.erdos_723.variants.eq_12
statement: True ↔ ∃ P L x x_1 x_2 pp, Configuration.ProjectivePlane.order P L = 12
summary: It is open whether there exists a projective plane of order 12.

title: Erdos726.erdos_726
statement:
True ↔
  Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop
    (fun n => ∑ p ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with Nat.Prime p ∧ ↑p / 2 < ↑n % ↑p, 1 / ↑p) fun n =>
    Real.log (Real.log ↑n) / 2
summary:
As $n\to \infty$ ranges over integers
$\sum_{p\leq n}1_{n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}}\frac{1}{p}\sim \frac{\log\log n}{2}$?

A conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75].

By $n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}$ we mean $n\equiv r\pmod{p}$ for some integer $r$ with $p/2<r<p$.

title: Erdos749.erdos_749
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ ε > 0, ∃ A, 1 - ε ≤ (A + A).lowerDensity ∧ (Nat.cast ∘ AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep A) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => 1
summary:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$
such that the lower density of $A+A$ is at least $1-\epsilon$
and yet $1_A\ast 1_A(n) \ll_\epsilon 1$ for all $n$?

title: Erdos770.erdos_770.parts.i
statement: True ↔ ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∃ a, {n | Erdos770.h n = ↑p}.HasDensity a
summary: For every prime `p`, does the density of integers with `h n = p` exist?

title: Erdos770.erdos_770.variants.three
statement: {n | Erdos770.h n = 3}.Infinite
summary: It is probably true that `h n = 3` for infinitely many `n`.

title: Erdos774.erdos_774
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite → A.IsProportionatelyDissociated → ∃ T, (∀ S ∈ T, S.IsDissociated) ∧ T.Finite ∧ A = ⋃₀ T
summary:
Is every proportionately dissociated (infinite) set the union of a finite
number of dissociated sets?

title: Erdos779.erdos_779
summary:
A Conjecture of Marian Deaconescu, see p.120 in https://doi.org/10.2307/2975810

[Needed to index shift in order to avoid trivial case $n = 0$,
where the conjecture is trivially false.]

title: Erdos789.erdos_789.variants.sq
statement: (fun n => ↑(Erdos789.subsetSumThreshold n)) =Θ[Filter.atTop] fun n => √↑n
summary:
Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$
then there is $B\subseteq A$ with $\lvert B\rvert \geq h(n)$ such that if
$a_1+\cdots+a_r=b_1+\cdots+b_s$ with $a_i,b_i\in B$ then $r=s$.

Is $h(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n})$?

title: Erdos812.erdos_812.parts.i
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ c > 0,
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ↑(Combinatorics.hypergraphRamsey 2 (n + 1)) / ↑(Combinatorics.hypergraphRamsey 2 n) ≥ 1 + c
summary: Is it true that $\frac{R(n+1)}{R(n)}\geq 1+c$ for some constant $c>0$, for all large $n$?

title: Erdos82.erdos_82
statement: Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos82.F n) / Real.log ↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary: $F(n) / \log n \to \infty as n \to \infty$

title: Erdos821.erdos_821
statement: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, {n | ↑(Erdos821.g n) > ↑n ^ (1 - ε)}.Infinite
summary:
Is it true that, for every $\epsilon>0$, there exist infinitely many $n$ such that
$g(n) > n^{1-\epsilon}$?

summary:
Is it true that, for any $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$\phi(n) | n + a$$?

statement: True ↔ ∀ n > 1, n.totient ∣ n - 1 ↔ Prime n
summary: When $n > 1$, Lehmer conjectured that $\phi(n) | n - 1$ if and only if $n$ is prime.

title: Erdos835.erdos_835

Does there exist a $k>2$ such that the $k$-sized subsets of {1,...,2k} can be coloured with
$k+1$ colours such that for every $A\subset \{1,\ldots,2k\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=k+1$ all $k+1$
colours appear among the $k$-sized subsets of $A$?

title: Erdos849.erdos_849
statement: True ↔ ∀ t ≥ 1, ∃ a, {n | ∃ k ≥ 1, 2 * k ≤ n ∧ n.choose k = a}.ncard = t
summary:
Is it true that, for every integer $t\geq1$, there is some integer $a$ such that ${n \choose k} = a$
with $1\leq k \le \frac{n}{2}$ has exactly $t$ solutions?

title: Erdos85.erdos_85
statement: True ↔ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos85.f n ≤ Erdos85.f (n + 1)
summary: Is it true that, for all large $n$, $f(n + 1) \ge f(n)$?

title: Erdos853.erdos_853.parts.i

Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $r(x)$ be the smallest even
integer $t$ such that $d_n = t$ has no solutions for $n \le x$.

Is it true that $r(x) \to \infty$?

title: Erdos853.erdos_853.parts.ii
statement: Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos853.r n) / Real.log ↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $r(x)$ be the smallest even
integer $t$ such that $d_n = t$ has no solutions for $n \le x$.

Is it true that $r(x) / \log x \to \infty$?

title: Erdos859.erdos_859
statement:
∃ c₁ > 0,

title: Erdos873.erdos_873
statement: True ↔ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ ε > 0, 0 < a 0 → StrictMono a → ∃ k, ∀ X > 0, ↑↑(Erdos873.F a X k) < ↑(X ^ ε)

Let $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and let $F(A,X,k)$ count the number of $i$
such that $[a_i,a_{i+1}, \dots ,a_{i+k−1}] < X$, where the left-hand side is the least common
multiple. Is it true that, for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists some $k$ such that
$F(A,X,k) < X^\epsilon$?

title: Erdos885.erdos_885
statement: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∃ Ns, (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧ Ns.card = k ∧ (⋂ n ∈ Ns, Erdos885.factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ k
summary:
Is it true that, for every $k \geq 1$, there exist integers $N_1 < \dots < N_k$ such that
$|\cap_i D(N_i)| \geq k$?

title: Erdos886.erdos_886
statement: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∃ K, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (Erdos886.Erdos886Divisors n ε 1).card ≤ K
summary:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Is it true that, for all large $n$, the number of divisors of $n$ in
$(n^{1/2},n^{1/2}+n^{1/2-\epsilon})$ is $O_\epsilon(1)$?

Erdős attributes this conjecture to Ruzsa.

title: Erdos887.erdos_887.parts.ii
statement: ∃ K, ∀ C > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, {d ∈ Finset.Ioo ⌊√↑n⌋₊ ⌈√↑n + C * ↑n ^ (1 / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n}.card ≤ K
summary:
Is there an absolute constant $K$ such that, for every $C > 0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
$n$ has at most $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + C n^{\frac{1}{4}})$.

title: Erdos889.erdos_889
statement: Filter.Tendsto Erdos889.v₀ Filter.atTop (nhds ⊤)
summary:
Let $v(n,k)$ count the prime factors of $n+k$ which
do not divide $n+i$ for $0\leq i < k$. Is it true that
$v_0(n)=\max_{k\geq 0}v(n,k)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$?

title: Erdos889.erdos_889.variants.general
statement: ∀ (l : ℕ), Filter.Tendsto (Erdos889.v_l l) Filter.atTop (nhds ⊤)
summary:
Let $v_l(n) = \max_{k\geq l} v(n,k)$. For every fixed $l$,
$v_l(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$

[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.

title: Erdos89.erdos_89
statement: (fun n => ↑n / √(Real.log ↑n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(EuclideanGeometry.minimalDistinctDistances n)
summary:
Erdős [Er46] asked whether every set of $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$
determines $\gg \frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$ many distinct distances.

title: Erdos890.erdos_890.parts.a
statement: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, Filter.liminf (fun n => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, ↑(Erdos890.omegaGt k (n + i))) Filter.atTop ≤ ↑k
summary:
If $\omega_k(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ which are $>k$, then is it true
that, for every $k\geq 1$,
$$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega_k(n+i)\leq k?$$

title: Erdos890.erdos_890.parts.b
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 1,
    Filter.limsup
        (fun n =>
          (∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, ↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n + i))) *
            (↑(Real.log (Real.log ↑n)) / ↑(Real.log ↑n)))
        Filter.atTop =
      1
summary:
Is it true that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\left(\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\right) \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1,$$
where $\omega$ counts the number of distinct prime factors without restriction?

title: Erdos891.erdos_891
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 2,
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∃ m ∈ Finset.Ico n (n + ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i), k < ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors m
summary:
Let $2=p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes and $k\geq 2$. Is it true that, for all sufficiently large
$n$, there must exist an integer in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k)$ with $>k$ many prime factors?

title: Erdos893.erdos_893
statement: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos893.f (2 * n)) / ↑(Erdos893.f n)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
Does the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{f(2n)}{f(n)}$ tend to infinity?

(Other finite limits have been ruled out by [KoLu25], see below)

title: Erdos9.erdos_9
statement: True ↔ 0 < Erdos9.Erdos9A.upperDensity
summary:
Is the upper density of the set of odd numbers that cannot be expressed as a prime plus
two powers of 2 positive?

title: Erdos91.erdos_91
statement: (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ¬Erdos91.UniqueMinimizer n) ↔ True
summary:
Suppose $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ has $\lvert A\rvert=n$ and minimises the number of distinct
distances between points in $A$. Prove that for large $n$ there are at least two
(and probably many) such $A$ which are non-similar.

title: Erdos912.erdos_912
statement: ∃ c > 0, Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(Erdos912.h n)) fun n => c * (↑n / Real.log ↑n) ^ (1 / 2)
summary:
Prove that there exists some $c>0$ such that
$$h(n) \sim c \left(\frac{n}{\log n}\right)^{1/2}$$
as $n\to \infty$.

title: Erdos912.erdos_912.variants.tao
statement: Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(Erdos912.h n)) fun n => √(2 * Real.pi) * (↑n / Real.log ↑n) ^ (1 / 2)
summary:
A heuristic of Tao using the Cramér model for the primes suggests this is true with
$c=\sqrt{2\pi}$.

display_title: Erdős problem 913 - infinite many 8 p sq sub one primes

title_parts.qualifier: infinite many 8 p sq sub one primes

title: Erdos913.erdos_913.variants.infinite_many_8p_sq_sub_one_primes
statement: {p | Nat.Prime p ∧ Nat.Prime (8 * p ^ 2 - 1)}.Infinite
summary: It is likely that there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $8p^2 - 1$ is also prime.

title: Erdos930.erdos_930
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ r > 0,
    ∃ k,
      ∀ (I₁ I₂ : Fin r → ℕ),
        (∀ (i : Fin r), 0 < I₁ i ∧ I₁ i + k ≤ I₂ i + 1) →
          (∀ (i j : Fin r), i < j → I₂ i < I₁ j) → ¬Erdos930.IsPower (∏ i, ∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc (I₁ i) (I₂ i), m)
summary:
Is it true that, for every $r$, there is a $k$ such that
if $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ are disjoint intervals of consecutive integers,
all of length at least $k$, then
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq r}\prod_{m\in I_i}m
$$
is not a perfect power?

title: Erdos931.erdos_931
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (k₁ k₂ : ℕ),
    k₂ ≥ 3 →
      k₂ ≤ k₁ →
        {(n₁, n₂) |
            n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧
              (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Finite
summary:
Let $k_1 \geq k_2 \geq 3$. Are there only finitely many $n_2\geq n_1 + k_1$
such that
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq k_1}(n_1 + i)\ \text{and}\ \prod_{1\leq j\leq k_2} (n_2 + j)
$$
have the same prime factors?

title: Erdos932.erdos_932
statement:
{r |
    2 ≤
      {m ∈ Finset.Ioo (Nat.nth Nat.Prime r) (Nat.nth Nat.Prime r.succ) |

summary:
Let $p_k$ denote the $k$th prime. For infinitely many $r$ there are at least two
integers $p_r < n < p_{r+1}$ all of whose prime factors are $< p_{r + 1} - p_r$.

title: Erdos933.erdos_933
statement: True ↔ Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑↑(2 ^ Erdos933.k n * 3 ^ Erdos933.l n) / (↑↑n * ↑(Real.log ↑n))) Filter.atTop = ⊤
summary:
If $n(n+1)=2^k3^lm$, where $(m,6)=1$, then is it true that
$\limsup_{n\to \infty} \frac{2^k3^l}{n\log n}=\infty$?

title: Erdos936.erdos_936.variants.factorial_add_one
statement: True ↔ Erdos936.EventuallyNotPowerful fun x => x.factorial + 1
summary: Is $n! + 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?

title: Erdos936.erdos_936.variants.factorial_sub_one

summary: Is $n! - 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?

statement: True ↔ Erdos936.EventuallyNotPowerful fun x => 2 ^ x - 1
summary: Is $2^n - 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?

title: Erdos942.erdos_942
statement:
True ↔

          {n | ↑(Erdos942.erdos_942.h n) > Real.log ↑n ^ (c - o n)}.Infinite
summary:
Is there some constant $c > 0$ such that $h(n) < (\log n)^{c + o(1)}$ and, for infinitely many $n$,
$h(n) > (\log n)^{c - o(1)}$.

title: Erdos943.erdos_943
statement: True ↔ ∃ o, o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Nat.Powerful n) ≤ ↑n ^ o n

title: Erdos944.erdos_944
statement: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 4, ∀ r ≥ 1, ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G k r
summary:
Let $k \ge 4$ and $r\ge 1$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>r$?

title: Erdos945.erdos_945

summary: Is it true that $F(x) \leq (\log x)^{O(1)}$?

title: Erdos949.erdos_949
statement: True ↔ ∀ (S : Set ℝ), (∀ a ∈ S, ∀ b ∈ S, a + b ∉ S) → ∃ A ⊆ Sᶜ, Cardinal.mk ↑A = Cardinal.continuum ∧ A + A ⊆ Sᶜ
summary:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a set containing no solutions to $a + b = c$.
Must there be a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R} \setminus S$ of cardinality continuum such that
$A + A \subseteq \mathbb{R}\setminus S$?

title: Erdos950.erdos_950.parts.i
statement: True ↔ Filter.liminf (fun n => ↑(Erdos950.f n)) Filter.atTop = 1
summary: Is it true that $\liminf f(n)=1$?

title: Erdos950.erdos_950.parts.ii
statement: True ↔ Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑(Erdos950.f n)) Filter.atTop = ⊤
summary: Is it true that $\limsup f(n)=\infty$?

statement: True ↔ Erdos950.f =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => Real.log (Real.log ↑n)
summary: Is it true that $f(n)=o(\log\log n)$ for all $n$?

statement:
True ↔

title: Erdos952.erdos_952
statement: True ↔ ∃ x C, Function.Injective x ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), Prime (x n) ∧ Zsqrtd.norm (x (n + 1) - x n) < C
summary:
Is there an infinite sequence of distinct Gaussian primes $x_1,x_2,\ldots$
such that $\lvert x_{n+1}-x_n\rvert \ll 1$?

title: Erdos96.erdos_96
statement: True ↔ (fun n => ↑(Erdos96.maxConvexUnitDistances n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n
summary:
If $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then there are $O(n)$ many pairs which are
distance $1$ apart.

title: Erdos962.erdos_962
statement:
True ↔
  ∃ ε,
    (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧

summary:

$\log k(n) \le (\log n)^{(1/2 + o(1))}$

title: Erdos972.erdos_972
statement: True ↔ ∀ α > 1, Irrational α → (Erdos972.primeSet α).Infinite
summary:
**Erdős problem 972.**
Let $\alpha > 1$ be irrational. Are there infinitely many primes $p$
such that $\lfloor p\alpha \rfloor$ is also prime?

title: Erdos975.erdos_975
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ (f : Polynomial ℤ),
    f.natDegree ≠ 0 →
      Irreducible f →
        (∀ᶠ (n : ℤ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ Polynomial.eval n f) →
          ∃ c > 0, Filter.Tendsto (fun x => Erdos975.Erdos975Sum f x / (x * Real.log x)) Filter.atTop (nhds c)
summary:
For an irreducible polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(n) \ge 1$ for sufficiently large $n$,
does there exists a constant $c = c(f) > 0$ such that
$\sum_{n \le x} \tau(f(n)) \approx c \cdot x \log x$?

Note that it is unclear whether the polynomial should have integer coefficients or merely be
integer-valued. We assume the former.

title: Erdos978.erdos_978.parts.ii
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ {f : Polynomial ℤ},
    Irreducible f →
      f.natDegree > 3 →
        (¬∃ l, f.natDegree = 2 ^ l) →
          0 < f.leadingCoeff →
            (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∃ n, ¬↑p ^ (f.natDegree - 2) ∣ Polynomial.eval (↑n) f) →

summary:
If $k>3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), and for all primes $p$ there exists $n$ such that $p^{k-2}\nmid f(n)$,
then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is $(k-2)$-power-free?

title: Erdos978.erdos_978.parts.iii
statement: True ↔ {n | Squarefree (n ^ 4 + 2)}.Infinite
summary: Does `n ^ 4 + 2` represent infinitely many squarefree numbers?

title: Erdos979.erdos_979
statement: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 2, Filter.limsup (fun n => (Erdos979.solutionSet n k).encard) Filter.atTop = ⊤
summary:
Let $k ≥ 2$, and let $f_k(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n = p_1^k + \dots + p_k^k$,
where the $p_i$ are prime numbers. Is it true that $\limsup f_k(n) = \infty$?

title: Erdos98.erdos_98
statement: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos98.h n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
summary:
Let $h(n)$ be such that any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line
and no four on a circle, determine at least $h(n)$ distinct distances. Does
$h(n)/n\to \infty$?

title: Erdos982.erdos_982
statement:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  3 ≤ n →

summary:
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then some vertex has at least
$\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ different distances to other vertices.

title: Erdos985.erdos_985
statement: True ↔ ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ≠ 2 → ∃ q, Nat.Prime q ∧ q < p ∧ orderOf ↑q = p - 1
summary: Is it true that, for every prime $p$, there is a prime $q \leq p$ which is a primitive root modulo $p$?

title: Erdos99.erdos_99
statement:
True ↔

        Erdos99.HasMinDist1 A →

summary:
For sufficiently large n, is it the case that any set of n points with minimum distance $1$
that minimizes diameter must contain an equilateral triangle of side length 1?

title: Green12.green_12

Let $G$ be an abelian group of size $N$, and suppose that $A \subset G$ has density $\alpha$.
Are there at least $\alpha^{15} N^{10}$ tuples $(x_1, \dots, x_5, y_1, \dots, y_5) \in G^{10}$
such that $x_i + y_j \in A$ whenever $j \in \{i, i+1, i+2\}$?

title: Green15.green_15
statement: True ↔ ∃ K f, LipschitzWith K f ∧ {x | ∃ n, (↑n, f n) = x}.IsAPOfLengthFree 3
summary:
Does there exist a Lipschitz function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose graph
$\Gamma = \{(n, f(n)) : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^2$ is free of 3-term progressions?

title: Green18.green_18
statement:
True ↔
  ∀ α > 0,
    ∃ c > 0,
      ∃ m₀,
        ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : Fintype G] [inst_2 : DecidableEq G] (A : Finset (G × G)),
